# Independent audit: feasible enlargements, face tents, and support contact

Audited `candidate 9d3ac163e4b5a3f7` in full and all six sections of `candidate 6e9992972c414d73`. **PASS.** The two wording clarifications recorded below were requested and applied. The actual geometric arguments and all constants are correct. No freely available boundary motion or negative cost is inferred.

## 1. Exact-signature enlargement in every dimension

The uniform strict signature makes the added-cap contribution exactly delta times its indicator for every nearby meeting point. Proper A and K sections give the required C1 original cap functions. Their Jacobian in (y,q) is invertible: multiplying a kernel relation by 1/s_i and summing first annihilates the common q component, and spanning then annihilates y. The implicit-function theorem therefore gives one actual moving source and the stated derivative p_I.

The middle caps cover the whole space. Endpoint depths equal ordinary depths by finite tilt isolation. Adding delta mass bounds the new ordinary depth at EVERY point by its old depth plus delta, so newly added candidate centers cause no gap. Old depth is zero outside the original body by separation, and on its boundary by a supporting hyperplane of zero d-volume. Thus m_A+delta bounds the new endpoint maximum. A's strict gap persists, and p_I>0 makes the common budget exceed a possibly tied, unchanged B maximum. The normalized derivative and sufficient strict cost inequality are therefore valid.

For a polytope facet, an outward apex sufficiently close to a relative-interior point violates only that facet inequality. Every segment from the apex into A enters through that facet; hence the added region is exactly the pyramid over the entire facet. The uniform signature survives throughout that pyramid. The volume epsilon H_(d-1)(F)/d and compatibility through the actual feasible body E are exact, including d=1. The theorem correctly does not make the same availability claim for arbitrary vertices.

## 2. General planar face bulges and the o(epsilon) remainder

The face is the whole supporting segment, so the upper boundary f has zero set exactly [alpha,beta]. The left supporting ray from (t,epsilon) can be chosen by MINIMIZING (epsilon-f(s))/(t-s) over old coordinates s<=alpha; the denominator is bounded away from zero, and compactness gives a contact. Its slope m is nonnegative and no more than epsilon/(t-alpha). The supporting-line identity yields (5). Thus its contact height tends to zero, its contact coordinate tends to alpha, and that height is o(epsilon). The analogous right statement is valid. This proves uniform convergence of the rescaled upper boundary on F to the stated tent.

The global inclusion A_epsilon subset A+[0,epsilon n] is correct because the latter convex set contains both A and the new point. It prevents lower-boundary gains and bounds each upper-section gain by epsilon. The outside-face visible widths tend to zero, so their area is o(epsilon). Concavity also keeps their old and new boundary heights between the two o(epsilon) contact heights and epsilon. This proves the total area expansion and the uniform thin-band control needed later.

A proper cutting line cannot coincide with the supporting line of F. For a transverse line, bounded convergence on F gives its tent-weighted coefficient; threshold changes of size O(epsilon) affect an interval of length O(epsilon) and therefore area O(epsilon^2), while the entire exterior-face remainder is already o(epsilon). For a parallel proper line, there is no added mass near the LINE, so its added-cap mass is locally constant in the threshold; that constant can be zero or the entire added area.

These two prose clarifications were requested and applied: use the minimum-slope construction on the left rather than an unqualified maximum-slope statement, and distinguish no mass near a parallel cutting line from no mass in its cap. Neither changes the proved formulas.

## 3. The actual moving menu without boundary-family differentiability

The added region lies in a horizontal band of height epsilon+o(epsilon). A transverse cutting line intersects such a band in length O(epsilon), uniformly in its threshold, so coarea gives a vanishing Lipschitz constant for the added-cap functions. A parallel proper cut has a fixed gap from the band in a fixed neighborhood of the original source and gives a constant added-cap function. The original map G is a local C1 diffeomorphism by the same weighted Jacobian argument as above.

Its inverse composed with the negative added-cap vector maps a sufficiently large O(epsilon) ball into itself and is a contraction, because the inverse derivative is bounded and the added-cap Lipschitz constants tend to zero. This supplies an actual fixed point, not just a formal first-order source. Expanding at that point and summing with the original weights gives (7).

The original A caps cover the whole plane: their thresholds sum to -sum h_B(v_i)<0, since an interior point of B has a strict support deficit in every normal and the normals sum to zero. Thus the weighted incidence W is everywhere at least min p_i>0. The first-order budget increment is strictly positive, and the tied B endpoint stays below the new menu. A's strict gap and the all-middle cover prove the asserted global upper certificate. Formula (8) retains the true added mass and the original denominator.

## 4. Finite tent optimization and interval concentration

Differentiating the two integral terms in (9) cancels the direct values of the piecewise constant cost and gives the displayed C'. On each interval of constant incidence, the constants A_0,B_0 yield (10). A stationary point exists exactly when their nonzero signs agree, with the displayed ratio of distances; if both vanish the cost is constant there, and if only one vanishes there is no isolated stationary point. Breakpoints and limits at available-interval endpoints complete the finite evaluation, while actual feasibility is still required.

For an interval [a,b] in the normalized face, a peak in that interval leaves excluded tent mass a^2/t+(1-b)^2/(1-t). Cauchy--Schwarz makes its minimum (1-(b-a))^2, attained at the stated interior peak when both exterior intervals have positive length. Moving an outside peak toward the interval increases its mass, so the optimum is global. Endpoint intervals give the same supremum by a one-sided limit; the entire face is immediate. This proves 2ell-ell^2 exactly. Substitution into the incidence-cost bound and rearrangement give (12)--(13), with positive denominators because p_i<r<=w_out. No actual length fraction or available peak is presumed.

## 5. Exact compatibility barrier on a face

The support representation of E is exact: x+B subset 2K is equivalent to u.x<=2h_K(u)-h_B(u) for every unit normal. If all these inequalities are strict at p, continuity on the compact unit sphere gives a uniform positive slack and hence an interior ball. Thus a boundary point has an active normal. Since A subset E, that normal also supports A at p.

At a relative-interior point of the nondegenerate face, both tangential directions lie in A, forcing any supporting normal to be perpendicular to the face; full dimension fixes its outward sign. Its only unit supporting normal is therefore n. This proves the exact equivalence in (14), for every relative-interior point of that face. Equality rules out all such feasible peaks; strict support slack permits all of them. With negative cost and the stated attained-local-minimum and global-depth hypotheses, strict slack would contradict the actual descent. Hence the shared support equality (15) is necessary. Actual midpoint inclusion then sends the Minkowski average of the two exposed faces into the exposed K face, which has positive length. No general shape classification follows.

## 6. A genuine curved-join calibration of the remainder

The o(epsilon) qualification is necessary for the stated generality. Consider the actual planar convex body with lower boundary y=-1 and upper boundary

    f(x)=0 for |x|<=1,
         -(|x|-1)^3 for 1<=|x|<=2.

Its whole top face is [-1,1] at height zero. Add the point (0,epsilon). For any small t>0 choose epsilon=3t^2+2t^3. The new right supporting line contacts the old curve at x=1+t, y=-t^3 and has slope -3t^2; the left side is its reflection. Direct integration gives the exact added area

    delta=epsilon+2t^3+(3/2)t^4.

The unit-height tent predicts epsilon. The excess is o(epsilon), but its ratio to epsilon^2 diverges as t tends to zero. Thus an O(epsilon^2) assertion for arbitrary convex curved joins would be false. For the proper cut x>=1/2, the exact added cap mass is

    epsilon/8+(3/4)t^3+(3/4)t^4,

which has exactly the source's coefficient and an o(epsilon), generally nonquadratic, remainder. This is an actual geometric calibration only; it does not claim that these cuts form a globally critical mixed-fiber menu.
